subject: MSA Security Exhibit: narrow-scope audit window & pen-test assertion language
content:
From: Procurement <procurement@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Counsel <legal@cardinalhealth.com>, AppSec <security@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarify MSA security exhibit: SOC 2 / pen test / audit window

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the recent demo — procurement here. Before we can move the order form to signature we need a couple clarifications on the MSA security exhibit:

- SOC 2: frequency and whether we can receive a copy of the full attestation or just a summary.
- Pen test / inspection language: we need to confirm the notice window and whether our pen test can be scoped to a specific product boundary (limited-scope).
- Audit rights: Cardinal Health prefers a defined cadence (once per 12 months) and an option to request one additional inspection in the case of a material incident.
- Evidence cadence: preference for a named owner and a delivery SLA for artifacts (e.g., 5 business days for logs / config snapshots).

Can you confirm what Redwood can commit to here and whether the security exhibit can be updated to reflect a constrained inspection (staging-only, business-hours, scoped systems)?

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Procurement Manager, Cardinal Health
procurement@cardinalhealth.com

---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Procurement <procurement@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify MSA security exhibit: SOC 2 / pen test / audit window

Hi Aisha — appreciate the clear list. Quick responses and a proposed path forward below.

SOC 2
- We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; for standard commercial MSA we include a Type II summary (attestation letter + control narrative excerpt). If Cardinal needs the full report we can accommodate under a mutual NDA and redaction process.

Pen test / inspection
- Redwood will accept a limited/scope inspection wording: "inspection limited to specified systems and staging environment". We propose a 14-calendar-day advance notice for non-emergency pen tests and a 5-business-day notice for evidence requests tied to routine audits.
- For live production testing, we require a written runbook and approval from our Site Reliability team; otherwise staging-only is the default.

Audit rights and cadence
- Proposed cadence: one bounded inspection per 12-month period, plus one ad-hoc follow-up inspection if triggered by a documented incident.
- All inspections will be subject to standard confidentiality and nondisclosure constraints and cannot exceed a combined 5 business days on-site/remote activity without prior agreement.

Evidence cadence and owners
- We'll assign an Evidence Owner (Security Operations) and commit to delivery SLAs: 5 business days for logs/config snapshots, 10 business days for deeper artifact requests requiring engineering pulls.

Next steps:
- Karthik will propose redline language for the security exhibit to capture the above. Jonas will add the technical constraints for production vs. staging. If those look good, I can send a redline to your counsel for sign-off.

Attachments: SOC2_Type_II_summary_2025.pdf (summary)

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 12:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify MSA security exhibit: SOC 2 / pen test / audit window

Grace — draft language below that I recommend we insert into the security exhibit (clean wording for procurement to review):

1) SOC2 Deliverable: Redwood will provide a SOC 2 Type II attestation summary annually. Full SOC 2 Type II reports may be provided under a mutual non-disclosure agreement; Redwood reserves the right to redact third-party vendor details and privileged content.

2) Limited-Scope Inspection: Customer may request a limited-scope inspection covering only the systems and deployment instances explicitly identified in the Order Form or an agreed inspection statement of work ("SOW"). Such inspection must be scoped to staging or non-production environments unless expressly agreed in writing.

3) Notice and Scheduling: Customer must provide at least 14 calendar days' advance notice for planned limited-scope penetration testing and 5 business days' notice for routine evidence requests. Emergency inspections triggered by a material security incident require reasonable notice and will be coordinated through Redwood's Security Ops.

4) Cadence and Incident Follow-up: Customer is entitled to one bounded inspection per rolling 12-month period. If a materially significant security incident occurs, Customer may request one additional inspection within 90 days of the incident.

5) Evidence SLA and Ownership: Redwood will designate an Evidence Owner and use commercially reasonable efforts to provide requested artifacts within 5 business days for standard logs/config exports and 10 business days for engineering-level artifacts. Any request that reasonably requires code changes, deep artifact pulls, or forensic imaging may be billed or require a separate SOW.

I kept the liability and billing carve-outs intentionally explicit so we don't commit to open-ended engineering time. Happy to tweak.

-Karthik
Associate General Counsel
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 13:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify MSA security exhibit: SOC 2 / pen test / audit window

Adding technical clarifications for the redline:
- "Staging" definition: isolated environment with production-like data sanitized; access via ephemeral credentials; no external traffic except approved test harnesses.
- Pen test rules of engagement: no high-risk destructive testing (DB writes, lateral movement to unrelated tenants). Allowed testing limited to OWASP Top 10 and agreed CVE verification steps.
- Evidence exports: logs will be provided in CSV/ndjson format when possible; for any request that requires restoring backups or full forensic capture we require an approved SOW and may need to schedule maintenance windows.

I support Karthik's SLAs but request we add a short clause about operational windows (business hours) and a limit of two concurrent evidence requests to avoid blocking platform operations.

-Jonas
Senior Security Engineer
jonas_weber@redwood.com

---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <procurement@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Legal Counsel <legal@cardinalhealth.com>, AppSec <security@cardinalhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jul 2025 14:38:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify MSA security exhibit: SOC 2 / pen test / audit window

Hi Aisha — thanks for the ask. Per our internal review we've agreed the following items to include in the security exhibit (summary):

- SOC 2: provide Type II summary with option for full report under NDA. (Attachment: SOC2_Type_II_summary_2025.pdf)
- Pen test: limited-scope to named systems / staging by default; 14-day notice for planned tests; production testing needs SRE-runbook sign-off.
- Audit cadence: one bounded inspection per 12 months + one ad-hoc within 90 days of a material incident.
- Evidence: Evidence Owner assigned; 5 business day SLA for standard logs, 10 for deeper artifacts; complex forensic captures require SOW.
- Operational constraints: business-hours only unless otherwise agreed; no more than two concurrent evidence pulls.

I've uploaded a proposed redline (draft_msa_redline_security_exhibit.docx) and a short internal ticket that captures the legal/ops alignment: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/LEGAL-412. If this matches your expectations I can send the redline to your counsel for a formal review.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
